newsitem.title: BRAZIL: RESEARCH ALERT-Telesp 12-month target price raised.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Telesp 12-month target price raised.

text.p: Morgan Stanley Dean Witter said it had raised to $440 its 12-month price target for Telesp, a unit of Brazilian telecom sytem Telebras serving Sao Paulo state.
- also said it had raised its 12-month price target for Telepar, a Telebras unit serving Parana state, to $1,000.
- Those target prices indicate upside potentials of 29 percent and 21 percent for Telesp and Telepar, respectively.

- Analyst Luiz Carvalho said in a report the target prices were revised to reflect positive impact of two recent important developments in Brazil: the release of initial results of the Band B cellular selloff process and the passage of the General Telecommunications Law in Congress.

- Morgan Stanley also said it was revising its earnings estimates for the companies. For Telesp, rated as a strong buy, the brokerage's earnings estimates were revised down to $19.50 from $20.38 for 1997 and $24.35 for 1998 from $24.46.
- Regarding Telepar, rated as outperform, it raised its earniings estimates to $54.90 from $54.75 for 1997 and revised down its earnings estimates to $69.08 from $70.37 for 1998.

- Concerning Telerj and Telemig, rated as outperform and neutral respectively, the earnings estimates are: $6.51 for 1997, down from $9.86 previously, for Telerj and $15.37, up from $14.79, for Telemig.
- Telesp preferred was up 7.07 percent at 394 reais earlier on the Sao Paulo bolsa.
- Telepar preferred was up 3.37 percent at 920.01 reais.
- Telerj was 6.58 percent higher at 173.20 reais, while Telemig preferred was up 2.56 percent at 200 reais.
